data.lore: The chapter spans 410 CE to approximately 590 CE, covering the Departure of Rome and the Birth of the Heptarchy across three distinct sub periods. Roman Withdrawal and British Vacuum covers the 410 CE Roman departure, Pictish raids, Vortigern's fateful hiring of Germanic mercenaries, and the arrival of the first Anglo-Saxon warbands. Germanic Conquest and Migration covers the mass 6th century Germanic settlement, the burning of Romano-British settlements, and the retreat of native Britons to Wales and Cornwall. Heptarchy Formation and Pagan Society covers the crystallization of the seven kingdoms, the Bretwalda title, the harsh social hierarchy of early Anglo-Saxon society, and the austere Germanic paganism that would soon meet Christian missionaries.

Anne of Cleves was Thomas Cromwell's foreign policy gambit, collapsing when the alliance was no longer needed. Catherine Howard was a pawn of the conservative Howard faction, her fall destroying her sponsors. Catherine Parr served as caretaker and reconciler in the king's declining years. Each wedding and divorce functioned as political crisis management, with the king's physical decline mirroring the old order he shattered.

data.lore: Henry VIII marries Catherine of Aragon, initially with affection and mutual respect. Catherine is popular and defends the realm. She has six pregnancies, but only Princess Mary survives, leading to Henry's fear of civil war without a male heir. He becomes convinced this is divine punishment, fixating on Leviticus and deeming his marriage sinful. Anne Boleyn arrives, refusing to be a mistress and demanding the crown. Catherine refuses to enter a convent, declares her virginity before Henry, and appeals to Emperor Charles V, escalating the crisis. The aristocracy divides into factions, and Henry resolves to divorce at any cost in 1527.

data.lore: This template converts a first person Roman historical script (e.g., march, siege, battle aftermath, camp life, medical treatment, civilian trade, slave market) into a sequence of 10-second selfie vlog scenes in the visual style of an early 2000s home DV camcorder tape. Each script paragraph yields two scenes (N.1 and N.2) covering different moments, beats, or angles of the same paragraph. Each scene generates one PHOTO PROMPT (still reference for Nano Banana) and one VIDEO PROMPT (Veo 3.1 clip with native audio). The host is a fixed, fictional character, image-locked via a character sheet, never redescribed in text. Named secondary characters also have reference sheets or are described by role and period portraiture. Violence is handled with respectful distance, aftermath, or implication, with specific paragraph overrides for atrocities; blood, mud, wounds, and combat aftermath are acceptable. Dialogue is first-person, present tense, conversational English, 70-80 characters per scene, delivered directly into the lens, with consistent American accent. Silence is a valid choice. All other details are depicted historically and specifically.

pairs.title: PRIMARY BEAT
pairs.intent: The opening or main action of the paragraph. Whatever the host is doing at the moment the paragraph turns on. If the paragraph describes a march, this is him walking with the column behind him. If it describes a camp built, this is him swinging the entrenching tool. If it describes a wound treated, this is the moment the physician's probe touches the flesh. The host is engaged in the action, the crowd or environment behind him is active, the camera bobs with his motion where he moves.
pairs.frame: The host's face is at arm's length, close to lens. Only his extended arm or hand may be partially visible at the bottom edge.
pairs.people: The host, exact appearance as the attached character sheet. The crowd or environment behind him is active.
pairs.camera: Shot from the front facing camera the host is holding in his own hand at arm's length, at selfie distance. Camera height is wherever his hand naturally holds the camera, roughly at his own eye level when walking or standing, lower when kneeling, wherever the described action puts him. Camera motion is constant natural handheld tremor, breathing level stillness while stationary, or a walking bob synced to each footstep when the scene is in motion. Never smooth, never stabilized. The lens spec approximates a consumer early 2000s DV camcorder front facing lens: fixed focal length in the wide range, autofocus that hunts, limited dynamic range with blown highlights and lifted shadows, mild rolling shutter, mild lens breathing when focus shifts, subtle chromatic aberration on hot edges, faded consumer grade color reproduction.

data.color_palette: One sentence per sub period naming its dominant colors, tied to specific objects, materials, weather, or biology drawn from that sub period. Palette follows what the genre supports: rich saturated but naturalistic color at all times, with atmospheric depth from haze, mist, dust, or spray where the setting allows. Avoid theatrical or fantasy color grading, but do not flatten pale or muted subjects into monochrome either.
data.lighting: Opens with the default rule: natural daylight outdoors, warm candlelight, oil lamp, or hearth fire indoors, overcast, storm, snow, mist, or firelight where the script specifies weather or fire. Golden hour and blue hour ARE permitted for pure landscape, seascape, and terrain establishing shots without figures (Pairs 1, 3, 9, 11) when the paragraph plausibly supports it. Character and interaction scenes with figures use practical, overcast, ambient, or firelight only, never romanticized golden light on faces. Underwater scenes use filtered blue green daylight through water column with volumetric rays fading with depth. Deep interior scenes such as archives, vaults, and vast marble halls use practical lamp light with deep shadow. Then one sentence per sub period. Always closes with: "No dramatic sunbeams on figures. No fantasy lighting."
data.textures: One sentence per sub period listing tactile surfaces drawn from the script. Genre appropriate examples: for HISTORICAL, mail rings, boiled leather, oil rubbed stone, worn wool, parchment, weighed silver. For INSTITUTIONAL, polished marble, aged parchment, brushed metal, thick paper, gold leaf, dark hardwood, polished ceremonial silk. For WILDLIFE, wet fur, feather barbs, ice grain, sea salt residue, rock lichen, animal breath in cold air. For DEEP PREHISTORY, worn bone, hide with fat rubbed into it, chert edge, ochre powder, mammoth ivory, packed snow. For PALEO, scaled or feathered hide, damp earth, prehistoric plant fiber, packed dust of an old track. For COSMIC or GEOLOGICAL, blue ice grain, meteorite fusion crust, drill core cylinder, snow crust, exposed rock, lab bench matte.
data.image_rules: Open by declaring the genre and the sub period. Then describe environment, light source, textures, camera angle, and figures with the face policy or anatomical accuracy phrase.
data.video_rules: Motion continues naturally from the image. Environment Reaction moves only environment. Character moves only that figure. Group moves the collective, never a single isolated subject. Interaction moves only the small human or animal detail between two subjects. Signature holds with only the most essential restrained motion. One slow camera move only where permitted (locked, slow push in, slow pull out, slow lateral pan, or slow steady drone drift where aerial is permitted). Introduce nothing that contradicts the image. Include period and setting ambient sound from the pool above.
